and probability of selection of odd no. $= \dfrac{4}{7}$

$= \dfrac{53}{105}$

11741.text: The coefficient of variation and standard deviation of an ungrouped data are 60 and 21 respectively. If 15 is added to every observation of the data, then the coefficient of variation of the new data is
11741.sol:
According to the given information, Coefficient of variance $(\mathrm{CV})=\frac{\sigma}{\mu} \times 100$
Where $\sigma$ is standard deviation and $\mu$ is mean of an ungrouped data.
$\because \quad \frac{\sigma}{\mu} \times 100=60$ and $\sigma=21$
So, $\quad \mu=\frac{21 \times 10}{6}=35$
After adding 15 to each observation of the data, the new mean $\mu^{\prime}=35+15=50$ but
$\Sigma\left|\mu^{\prime}-x_i^{\prime}\right|=\Sigma\left|\mu-x_i\right|$, [where $x_i^{\prime}=x_i+15$ ]
Now, $\sigma=\sqrt{\frac{\sum\left(\mu-x_i\right)^2}{n}}=21\Rightarrow \Sigma\left(\mu-x_i\right)^2=(21)^2 \times n$
So, new standard deviation $\sigma^{\prime}=\sqrt{\frac{\sum\left(\mu^{\prime}-x_i^{\prime}\right)^2}{n}}=\sqrt{\frac{(21)^2 \times n}{n}}=21 $\therefore$ New coefficient of variance =\frac{\sigma^{\prime}}{\mu^{\prime}} \times100=\frac{21}{50} \times100=21 \times2=42 Hence, option (b) is correct.$

16028.text: The bob of a simple pendulum is a spherical hollow ball filled with water. A plugged hole near the bottom of the oscillating bob gets suddenly unplugged. During observation, till water is coming out, the time period of oscillation would:
options: first increase and then decrease to the original value.
first decrease and then increase to the original value.
16028.sol:
The time period of the simple pendulum is, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$ Here, $l$ is the effective length of the pendulum up to& centre of mass.

When the hole at bottom of the hollow sphere (bob) filled with& water is unplugged, the water will drain from the bob due to which the centre of mass will shift downward, therefore, the length of the pendulum& will slightly increase, which will lead to increase in time period.

After the water completely drained out the centre of mass again shift to its original position that is up to the centre of the hollow sphere (bob) due to which the length of the pendulum will decrease and will reach to its initial state which causes the time period to reach its original value.

19542.subject: Chemistry
19542.text: Propanal on reaction with dilute NaOH, undergoes aldol condensation resulting in the formation of a compound A. Identify the correct structure of A and name of the compound.
19542.sol:
Propanal (CH_3-CH_2-CHO$) undergoes self-aldol condensation in the presence of dilute NaOH.

The \alpha$-carbon of one propanal molecule is deprotonated by the base to form an enolate ion:
$CH_3-CH_2-CHO + OH^- \rightleftharpoons CH_3-\bar{C}H-CHO + H_2O$

This enolate ion acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of a second propanal molecule:
$CH_3-CH_2-CHO + CH_3-\bar{C}H-CHO \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH(O^-)-CH(CH_3)-CHO$

Protonation of the resulting alkoxide ion from water yields the aldol product (Compound A):
$CH_3-CH_2-CH(O^-)-CH(CH_3)-CHO + H_2O \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH(CH_3)-CHO + OH^-$

To name this compound according to IUPAC rules, we select the longest carbon chain containing the aldehyde group, which has 5 carbon atoms (pentanal). Numbering starts from the aldehyde carbon:
C1: $-CHO$
C2: $-CH(CH_3)-$
C3: $-CH(OH)-$
C4: $-CH_2-$
C5: $-CH_3$

There is a methyl group at C2 and a hydroxy group at C3. Thus, the IUPAC name is 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal. This matches the structure and name given in option (D).

Answer: 3-hydroxy-2-methyl-pentanal

Leucine and Tryptophan are indeed classified as essential amino acids, as they cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through the diet. Therefore, the second statement is correct.

Curdling of milk involves the denaturation of casein protein due to the change in pH caused by lactic acid production, which alters the protein structure. Thus, it is a denaturation process, making the third statement incorrect.

Invert sugar is an equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose obtained by the hydrolysis of sucrose. Fructose itself is a monosaccharide and not an invert sugar. Therefore, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Answer: Leucine and Tryptophan are classified as Essential amino acids

20057.subject: Chemistry
20057.text: The basic character of transition metal monoxides follows the order:
20057.sol:
For transition metal oxides in the same oxidation state, the basic character decreases as we move from left to right across a period.

This occurs because the effective nuclear charge increases and the ionic radius of the metal ion decreases (Ti^{2+} > V^{2+} > Cr^{2+} > Fe^{2+}$). The decrease in size increases the polarizing power of the cation, leading to an increase in the covalent character of the metal-oxygen bond and a corresponding decrease in the basic character.

The atomic numbers of the given metals are $Ti$ (22$), $V$ (23$), $Cr$ (24$), and $Fe$ (26$).

Therefore, the correct order of basic character is $TiO > VO > CrO > FeO$.

Answer: $TiO > VO > CrO > FeO

20169.text:
The reaction taking place in a galvanic cell is as given
$\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{B}^{2+}\left(\mathrm{1} \mathrm{1} \mathrm{1 0} \mathrm{0}^{-\mathrm{M}} \mathrm{M}\right) \rightarrow \mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{A}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M}).$
The emf of the cell is $+2.651 \mathrm{ V}$. If the standard emf of the cell is $+2.71 \mathrm{ V}$, what is the value of $\mathrm{X}$ ?
20169.sol:
The cell reaction is $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{B}^{2+}(10^{-X} \mathrm{M}) \rightarrow \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{A}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M})$.

The Nernst equation for the cell at $298 \mathrm{K}$ is given by $E_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log Q$, where $n$ is the number of electrons transferred.

Here, $n = 2$, $E_{\text{cell}} = 2.651 \mathrm{ V}$, and $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = 2.71 \mathrm{ V}$.

The reaction quotient $Q$ is $\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}^{2+}]}{[\mathrm{B}^{2+}]} = \dfrac{0.1}{10^{-X}} = 10^{X-1}$.

Substituting the values into the Nernst equation:

$2.651 = 2.71 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log(10^{X-1})$

$2.651 - 2.71 = -0.02955 \times (X-1)$

$-0.059 = -0.02955 \times (X-1)$

$X-1 = \dfrac{0.059}{0.02955} \approx 2$

$X = 2 + 1 = 3$.

Answer: X = 3

20255.subject: Chemistry
20255.text: Give the correct order of acidity of
20255.sol:
The acidity of oxoacids of chlorine depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed after the loss of a proton. The conjugate bases are $\mathrm{ClO}_{4}^{-}$, $\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$, $\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}$, and $\mathrm{ClO}^{-}$.

The stability of these conjugate bases is determined by the number of oxygen atoms attached to the central chlorine atom. More oxygen atoms lead to greater delocalization of the negative charge through resonance, thereby increasing the stability of the conjugate base.

The number of oxygen atoms in the acids are: $\mathrm{HClO}_4$ (4), $\mathrm{HClO}_3$ (3), $\mathrm{HClO}_2$ (2), and $\mathrm{HClO}$ (1).

The stability order of the conjugate bases is $\mathrm{ClO}_{4}^{-} > \mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-} > \mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-} > \mathrm{ClO}^{-}$.

Since a more stable conjugate base corresponds to a stronger acid, the order of acidity is $\mathrm{HClO}_4 > \mathrm{HClO}_3 > \mathrm{HClO}_2 > \mathrm{HClO}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{HClO} < \mathrm{HClO}_2 < \mathrm{HClO}_3 < \mathrm{HClO}_4$

Finally, the reaction of iodobenzene with sodium in dry ether is the Fittig reaction: $2\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{I} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 - \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 + 2\mathrm{NaI}$. 20916.subject: Mathematics
20916.text: The absolute maximum and minimum values of the function $f(x) = \sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x$ in $[0, \pi]$ are
20916.sol:
Given $f(x) = \sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x$

We can rewrite the function as:

$f(x) = 2 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \sin x + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cos x \right) = 2 \sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

For $x \in [0, \pi]$, the angle $\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right]$.

The maximum value of $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ in this interval is $1$, which occurs at $x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Thus, the absolute maximum value of $f(x)$ is $2 \times 1 = 2$.

The minimum value of $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ in this interval occurs at the endpoint $x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3} \Rightarrow x = \pi$.

Thus, the absolute minimum value of $f(x)$ is $2 \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{3}$.

Alternatively, evaluating the function at the critical point $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and the endpoints $x = 0, \pi$:

$f(0) = \sqrt{3}$

$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 2$

$f(\pi) = -\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, the absolute minimum value is $-\sqrt{3}$ and the absolute maximum value is $2$.

Answer: Minimum value $= -\sqrt{3}$, maximum value $= 2$

21100.subject: Mathematics
21100.text: $Middle term in the expansion of \left(x^{2}+\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}+2\right)^{n}$ is
21100.sol:
The given expression is $\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{x^{2}} + 2\right)^{n}$.

This can be rewritten as $\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{2n}$.

The number of terms in the expansion of $\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{2n}$ is $2n + 1$, which is odd.

Therefore, there is only one middle term, which is the $\left(\dfrac{2n}{2} + 1\right)$-th term, i.e., the $(n+1)$-th term.

The general term $T_{r+1}$ in the expansion of $(a+b)^{m}$ is given by $^{m}C_{r} a^{m-r} b^{r}$.

For the $(n+1)$-th term, $r = n and m = 2n$.

$T_{n+1} = ^{2n}C_{n} (x)^{2n-n} \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{n} = ^{2n}C_{n} x^{n} \dfrac{1}{x^{n}} = ^{2n}C_{n}$.

The value of $^{2n}C_{n}$ is $\dfrac{(2n)!}{n!(2n-n)!} = \dfrac{(2n)!}{n!n!} = \dfrac{(2n)!}{(n!)^{2}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{(2 n) !}{(n !)^{2}}$

21182.subject: Mathematics
21182.sol:
Given the expression $\left[i^{22} + \left(\dfrac{1}{i}\right)^{25}\right]^3$.

First, simplify the powers of $i$. We know that $i^2 = -1$, $i^4 = 1$, and $\dfrac{1}{i} = -i$.

$i^{22} = (i^4)^5 \times i^2 = 1^5 \times (-1) = -1$.

$\left(\dfrac{1}{i}\right)^{25} = (-i)^{25} = (-1)^{25} \times i^{25} = -1 \times (i^4)^6 \times i = -1 \times 1^6 \times i = -i$.

Substituting these values into the expression:

$\left[-1 + (-i)\right]^3 = \left[-(1 + i)\right]^3 = -1 \times (1 + i)^3$.

Expanding $(1 + i)^3$ using the formula $(a + b)^3 = a^3 + b^3 + 3ab(a + b)$:

$(1 + i)^3 = 1^3 + i^3 + 3(1)(i)(1 + i) = 1 - i + 3i(1 + i) = 1 - i + 3i + 3i^2 = 1 + 2i - 3 = -2 + 2i$.

Finally, multiplying by $-1$:

$-1 \times (-2 + 2i) = 2 - 2i = 2(1 - i)$.

Answer: $2(1-i)$

21357.text: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=0$ represents
options: all straight lines in a plane
21357.sol:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{d^2 y}{d x^2} = 0$.

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$ once, we obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = c_1$, where $c_1$ is an arbitrary constant.

Integrating again with respect to $x$, we obtain $y = c_1 x + c_2$, where $c_2$ is another arbitrary constant.

The equation $y = c_1 x + c_2$ represents the general equation of a straight line in the Cartesian plane, where $c_1$ is the slope and $c_2$ is the y-intercept.

Answer: all straight lines in a plane

21618.subject: Mathematics
21618.sol:
The given expression is $E = \cot ^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}}\right) - \sec ^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right) - \operatorname{cosec}^{-1}(-1) - \tan ^{-1}(1)$.

Simplify the arguments:
$\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}$ and $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$.

Evaluate each term individually:
1. $\cot ^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = \pi - \cot ^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$.

2. $\sec ^{-1}(-\sqrt{2}) = \pi - \sec ^{-1}(\sqrt{2}) = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

3. $\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}(-1) = -\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}(1) = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

4. $\tan ^{-1}(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Substitute these values into the expression $E$:
$E = \dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{3\pi}{4} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Combine the terms:
$E = \dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{3\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{5\pi - 6\pi + 3\pi}{6} = \dfrac{2\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

21854.subject: Mathematics
21854.text: There are 12 points in a plane out of which 3 points are collinear. How many straight lines can be drawn by joining any two of them?
21854.sol:
The total number of ways to select 2 points out of 12 points is given by ^{12}C_{2}$.

^{12}C_{2} = \dfrac{12 \times 11}{2 \times 1} = 66$.

Since 3 points are collinear, joining any two of these 3 points results in the same line. The number of lines formed by these 3 points is ^{3}C_{2} = $\dfrac{3 \times 2}{2 \times 1} =3$.

These 3 lines are counted as distinct lines in the total ^{12}C_{2}$ calculation, but they actually represent only 1 single line. Therefore, we must subtract the 3 lines and add back the 1 line that represents the collinear set.

Total number of lines = ^{12}C_{2} - ^{3}C_{2} + 1 = 66 - 3 + 1 = 64$.

Answer: 64

21938.subject: Mathematics
21938.text: If the probability for $A$ to fail in an examination is 0.2 and that for $B$ is 0.3 , then the probability that either $A$ or $B$ fail is
21938.sol:
Let $P(A)$ be the probability that $A$ fails and $P(B)$ be the probability that $B$ fails. Given $P(A) = 0.2$ and $P(B) = 0.3$.

Since the events of $A$ and $B$ failing are independent, the probability that both fail is $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B) = 0.2 \times 0.3 = 0.06$.

The probability that either $A$ or $B$ fails is given by the addition theorem of probability: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$.

Substituting the values, we get $P(A \cup B) = 0.2 + 0.3 - 0.06 = 0.5 - 0.06 = 0.44$.

Answer: 0.44

22488.text: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is $400 \mathrm{ pF}$. It is connected to an ac source of $100 \mathrm{ V}$ having an angular frequency $100 \mathrm{ rad s}^{-1}$. If the rms value of the current is $4 \mu \mathrm{A}$, the displacement current is:
22488.sol:
The displacement current $I_d$ in a parallel plate capacitor is defined as the current flowing through the circuit, which is equal to the conduction current $I_c$ in the connecting wires.

The relationship between the conduction current and the displacement current is given by $I_d = I_c$.

Given that the rms value of the current in the circuit is $I_{rms} = 4 \mu \text{A}$, this current represents the conduction current flowing through the wires connected to the capacitor plates.

According to the principle of continuity of current, the displacement current between the plates of the capacitor must be equal to the conduction current in the external circuit.

Therefore, $I_d = I_{rms} = 4 \mu \text{A}$.

Answer: 4 $\mu$ A

25881.text: A straight line through the vertex $P$ of a $\triangle P Q R$ intersects the side $Q R$ at the point $S$ and the circumcircle of the $\triangle P Q R$ at the point $T$. If $S$ is not the centre of the circumcircle, then
25881.sol:
Let a straight line through the vertex $P$ of a given $\triangle P Q R$ intersects the side $Q R$ at the point $S$ and the circumcircle of $\triangle P Q R$ at the point $T$.
Points $P, Q, R, T$ are concyclic, hence
$ \begin{array}{rlrl}
P S \cdot S T & =Q S \cdot S R & & \\
\Rightarrow \quad P_1 & \geq 2 \sqrt{P S \cdot S T} & \\
& \text{ Now, } \frac{P S+S T}{2} & \geq \sqrt{P S \cdot S T} & {[\because \mathrm{AM} \geq \mathrm{GM}]}
\end{array} $

and $\quad \frac{1}{P S}+\frac{1}{S T} \geq \frac{2}{\sqrt{P S \cdot S T}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{Q S \cdot S R}}$
Also, $\quad \frac{S Q+Q R}{2} \geq \sqrt{S Q \cdot S R} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{Q R}{2} \geq \sqrt{S Q \cdot S R} \begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{\sqrt{S Q \cdot S R}} \geq \frac{2}{Q R} \Rightarrow \frac{2}{\sqrt{S Q \cdot S R}} \geq \frac{4}{Q R} \\
\text{ Hence, } & \frac{1}{P S}+\frac{1}{S T} \geq \frac{2}{\sqrt{Q S \cdot S R}} \geq \frac{4}{Q R} .
\end{array} $

29026.subject: Chemistry
29026.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Presence of large number of unpaired electrons in transition metal atoms results in higher enthalpies of their atomisation.
Statement II: $d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz} < d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2} < d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz}$ are the d-orbital splittings in $[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ and $[Ni(Cl)_4]^{2-}$ complex ions respectively.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
29026.sol:
Statement I: The enthalpy of atomisation of transition metals depends on the strength of metallic bonding. A greater number of unpaired electrons in the d-orbitals leads to stronger metallic bonding, which results in a higher enthalpy of atomisation. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Statement II: $[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ is an octahedral complex. In an octahedral crystal field, the d-orbitals split such that the $t_{2g}$ set of orbitals ($d_{xy}, d_{xz}, d_{yz}$) has lower energy than the $e_g$ set of orbitals ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}$). Therefore, $d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz} < d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2}$.

$[Ni(Cl)_4]^{2-}$ is a tetrahedral complex because $Cl^{-}$ is a weak field ligand and the coordination number is $4$. In a tetrahedral crystal field, the splitting is reversed compared to the octahedral field. The $e$ set of orbitals ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}$) has lower energy than the $t_2$ set of orbitals ($d_{xy}, d_{xz}, d_{yz}$). Therefore, $d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2} < d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz}$. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

29535.subject: Chemistry
options: Both ${NO}_{2}$ and ${SO}_{2}$ are present in classical smog
Photochemical smog has high concentration of oxidizing agents
Classical smog also has high concentration of oxidizing agents
29535.sol:
A. Classical smog occurs in cool humid climate. It is a mixture of smoke, fog, and sulphur dioxide. Chemically it is a reducing mixture and so it is called reducing smog. So statement A is incorrect.

B. Classical smog is a mixture of smoke, fog and ${SO}_{2}$. ${NO}_{2}$ is not present in classical smog. So, statement B is incorrect.

C. Photochemical smog occurs in warm, dry and sunny climate. The main components of the photochemical smog result from the action of sunlight on unsaturated hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides produced by automobiles and factories. Photochemical smog has high concentration of oxidising agents and is, therefore, called as oxidising smog. So, statement C is correct.

D. Classical smog is a reducing mixture, so it is called as reducing smog. Hence, statement D is incorrect.

32430.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as

Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R$.

Assertion $A$ : Finest gold is red in colour, as the size of the particles increases, it appears purple then blue and finally gold.

32430.sol:
The colour of colloidal solution depends on the wavelength of light scattered by the dispersed particles. The wavelength of light further depends on the size and nature of the particles. The colour of colloidal solution also changes with the manner in which the observer receives the light. For example, a mixture of milk and water appears blue when viewed by the reflected light and red when viewed by the transmitted light. Finest gold sol is red in colour; as the size of particles increases, it appears purple, then blue and finally golden.

Hence, Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

34287.text: Let $f$ be a non-negative function in $[ 0, 1 ]$ and twice differentiable in $( 0, 1 ) .$ If ${∫}_{0}^{x}\sqrt{1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( t )\right)}^{2}}dt = {∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt, 0 \le x \le 1$ and $f ( 0 ) = 0,$ then $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt:$
34287.sol:
Newton - Leibnitz rule

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({∫}_{f\left(x\right)}^{g\left(x\right)}h\left(x\right) d x\right) = g ' \left(x\right)h\left(g ( x )\right) - f ' \left(x\right)h\left(f ( x )\right)$

Given that

${∫}_{0}^{x}\sqrt{1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( t )\right)}^{2}}dt = {∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt$

Differentiate $w . r . t . x$

$\sqrt{1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( x )\right)}^{2}} = f ( x )$

Squaring on both sides
$⇒ 1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( x )\right)}^{2} = ( f ( x ) {)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left({f}^{'} ( x )\right)}^{2} = 1 - ( f ( x ) {)}^{2}$

$f\left(x\right) = y ⇒ f ' \left(x\right) = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

38057.text: The shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 6}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x - 6}{3} = \dfrac{1 - y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{0}$ is equal to ______
38057.sol:
Given equations are

$\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 6}{2}$ is passing through a point $\left(2, - 1, 6\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $3, 2, 2$.

So,

$\overset{\to}{a}1 = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\dfrac{x - 6}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{0}$ is passing through a point $\left(6, 1, - 8\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $3, - 2, 0$.

$\overset{\to}{a}2 = 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}2 = 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}$

Now,

$\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1 = 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = 4\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{16 + 36 + 144} = 14$

We know that the shortest distance between two skew lines is $\dfrac{\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right)\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right|}$

$= \left|\dfrac{\left(4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}\right)}{14}\right|$

$= \dfrac{\left|16 + 12 + 168\right|}{14} = 14$ units

38402.sol:
We have, $\sin^{2}10 ° \times sin20 ° \times sin40 ° \times sin50 ° \times sin70 °$

$= \left(sin10 ° \times sin50 ° \times sin70 °\right)\left(sin10 ° \times sin20 ° \times sin40 °\right)$

Using, $sin\theta = cos\left(90 ° - \theta\right)$

$= \left[cos80 ° \times cos40 ° \times cos20 °\right]\left[sin10 ° \times sin\left(30 ° - 10 °\right) \times sin\left(30 ° + 10 °\right)\right]$

We know that $cos\thetacos2\thetacos{2}^{2}\theta \ldots cos{2}^{n - 1}\theta = \dfrac{sin{2}^{n}\theta}{{2}^{n}sin\theta}$

and $sin\left(A + B\right) \cdot sin\left(A - B\right) = \sin^{2}A - \sin^{2}B$$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin{2}^{3}\left(20 °\right)}{{2}^{3}sin20 °}\right)\left[sin10 ° \times \left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \sin^{2}10 °\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin160 °}{{2}^{3}sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{sin10 ° - 4\sin^{3}10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin\left(180 ° - 20 °\right)}{8sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{3sin10 ° - 4\sin^{3}10 ° - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin20 °}{8sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{sin30 ° - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{1 - 4sin10 °}{8}\right) = \alpha - \dfrac{sin10 °}{16}$ (given)

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - 4sin10 °}{64} = \dfrac{16\alpha - sin10 °}{16}$

$⇒ 1 - 4sin10 ° = 64\alpha - 4sin10 °$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{64}$.

The quality factor of an L.C.R. circuit is given by,

(Quality factor) $Q = \dfrac{1}{R}\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{C}} . . . ( i )$

Where $L, R, C$ are the inductance, resistance, and conductance of the L.C.R. circuit. The given resonance frequency is, ${\text{\omega}}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$

$⇒ \sqrt{C} = \dfrac{1}{{\text{\omega}}_{0}\sqrt{L}} . . . ( ii )$

From $( i )$ and $( ii )$

$⇒ Q = \dfrac{1}{R}\sqrt{L} \times {\text{\omega}}_{0}\sqrt{L} ⇒ Q = \dfrac{{\text{\omega}}_{0}L}{R}$

40633.text: In finding the electric field using Gauss law the formula $\left|\overset{\to}{E}\right| = \dfrac{{q}_{enc}}{{ε}_{0}\left|A\right|}$ is applicable. In the formula ${ε}_{0}$ is permittivity of free space, $A$ is the area of Gaussian surface and ${q}_{enc}$ is charge enclosed by the Gaussian surface. This equation can be used in which of the following situation?
options: Only when the Gaussian surface is an equipotential surface
Only when the Gaussian surface is an equipotential surface and $\left|\overset{\to}{E}\right|$ is constant on the surface.
Only when $\left|\overset{\to}{E}\right| =$ constant on the surface.
For any choice of Gaussian surface.
40633.sol:
According to Gauss law of electrostatics, the electric flux through an enclosed surface is given by ${ϕ}_{E} = \dfrac{{q}_{enc}}{{ε}_{0}}$

From the formula of electric flux, $ϕ = \overset{\to}{E} \cdot d \overset{\to}{s}$

Also, the relation between electric field and electric potential is given by $V = \overset{\to}{E} \cdot d \overset{\to}{r}$

So, the formula $\left|\overset{\to}{E}\right| = \dfrac{{q}_{enc}}{{ε}_{0}\left|A\right|}$ is only applicable when the Gaussian surface is an equipotential surface and $\left|\overset{\to}{E}\right|$ is constant on the surface.

$\mathrm{T}=30.4^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}} \times 100=\frac{6.4}{30} \times 100=21 \%$

so the closest answer is $20 \%$.

43430.subject: Physics
43430.text: Two $4$ bits binary numbers, $A = 1101$ and $B = 1010$ are given in the inputs of a logic circuit shown in figure below. The output $(Y)$ will be:
43430.sol:
From the given logic circuit, the input $A$ passes through a NOT gate, giving $\overline{A}$.

This output $\overline{A}$ and the input $B$ are then fed into a NAND gate.

The Boolean expression for the final output $Y$ is:
$Y = \overline{\overline{A} \cdot B}$

Given the $4$-bit binary inputs:
$A = 1101$
$B = 1010$

First, find the bitwise NOT of $A$:
$\overline{A} = \overline{1101} = 0010$

Next, find the bitwise AND of $\overline{A}$ and $B$:
$\overline{A} \cdot B = 0010 \cdot 1010 = 0010$

Finally, apply the NOT operation for the NAND gate:
$Y = \overline{0010} = 1101$

Alternatively, using De Morgan's laws:
$Y = \overline{\overline{A} \cdot B} = A + \overline{B}$
$Y = 1101 + \overline{1010} = 1101 + 0101 = 1101$

Therefore, the output $Y$ is $1101$.

Answer: $Y = 1101$

48993.text: Area of a triangle formed by tangent and normal to the curve $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ at $p\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{b}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ with the $x$-axis is
48993.sol:
Given curve $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ and point $P\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{b}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
Slope of tangent at $P$ is $-b / a$.
Slope of normal at $P$ is $a / b$.
Equation of tangent on the curve
$$
b x+a y=\sqrt{2} a b
$$
Equation of normal on the tangent of the curve
$$
-a x+b y=\frac{\left(b^{2}-a^{2}\right)}{\sqrt{2}}
$$
Equation of $x$-axis $y=0$
Solving these equations in successive manner, we get three points of triangle
$\left(\frac{a^{2}-b^{2}}{a \sqrt{2}}, 0\right),(\sqrt{2} \cdot a, 0)$ and $\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{b}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
Now, area of triangle $=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\frac{a^{2}-b^{2}}{a \sqrt{2}} & 0 & 1 \\ a / \sqrt{2} \cdot a & 0 / \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right|$
$=\frac{-b}{2 \sqrt{2}}\left\{\frac{a^{2}-b^{2}}{a \sqrt{2}}-\sqrt{2} \cdot a\right\}=\frac{-b}{4 a}\left(-a^{2}-b^{2}\right)$
$=\frac{b\left(a^{2}+b^{2}\right)}{4 a}$

49171.subject: Mathematics
49171.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 - 1 & \text{if } x \geq 2 \\ x + 1 & \text{if } x < 2 \end{cases}$, then $\lim\limits_{x \to 1} f(x) + \lim\limits_{x \to 2} f(x) = $
49171.sol:
For $x \to 1$, since $x < 2$, the function is $f(x) = x + 1$.

$\lim\limits_{x \to 1} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 1} (x + 1) = 1 + 1 = 2$

For $x \to 2$, we evaluate the left-hand and right-hand limits.

Left-hand limit at $x = 2$:
$\lim\limits_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 2^-} (x + 1) = 2 + 1 = 3$

Right-hand limit at $x = 2$:
$\lim\limits_{x \to 2^+} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 2^+} (x^2 - 1) = 2^2 - 1 = 3$

Since the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit, $\lim\limits_{x \to 2} f(x) = 3$.

The required sum is $\lim\limits_{x \to 1} f(x) + \lim\limits_{x \to 2} f(x) = 2 + 3 = 5$.

Answer: $5$

50680.subject: Physics
50680.text:
A galvanometer of resistance \( 50 \Omega \) is connected to a battery of \( 3 $\mathrm{ V}$\) along with a resistance of
\( 2950 \Omega \) in series shows full-scale deflection of \( 30 \) divisions. The additional series resistance
required to reduce the deflection to \( 20 \) divisions is
50680.sol:
Given, galvanometer resistance, \( R_{G}=50 \Omega ; \) battery, \( $\mathrm{V}=$3 $\mathrm{~V}$; \) resistance, \( $\mathrm{R}=$2950 \Omega ; \) deflection \( =30 \) divisions. Now,
\( I=$\frac{V}{\left(R_{G}+R\right)}=\frac{3}{(50+2950)}=$0.001=1 $\times$10^{-3} $\mathrm{~A}$\)
Thus, current when deflection is \( 30 \) divisions \( =10^{-3} $\mathrm{~A}$\)
\( \Rightarrow \) Current when deflection is \( 1 \) division \( =$\frac{10^{-3}}{30}$\)
\( \Rightarrow \) Current when deflection is \( 20 \) division \( =$\frac{10^{-3}}{30} \times$20 \)
Therefore, in order to have a deflection of \( 20 \) division the resistance should be
\[ $\begin{array}{l}\frac{2}{3} \times$10^{-3}=$\frac{3}{(50+R)}$\\ \Rightarrow(50+R)=$\frac{3 \times 3}{2 \times 10^{-3}}$\\ 50+R=4.5 $\times$1000 \\ R=4500-50=4450 \end{array} \]
Hence, additional resistance required \( =4450-2950=1500 \)

55253.subject: Chemistry
55253.text: Identify false statement from following regarding preparation of amines by Hofmann degradation method.
options: It is useful to convert amides to primary amines.
In this -CO-group is reduced to $-\text{CH}_2-$ group.
Molar mass of the amine obtained is always less than the amide.
55253.sol:
Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction is used for the conversion of primary amides to primary amines with one carbon atom less than the original amide.

The general reaction is:
$R-CO-NH_2 + Br_2 + 4KOH \rightarrow R-NH_2 + K_2CO_3 + 2KBr + 2H_2O$

In this reaction, the carbonyl group ($-CO-$) is lost as potassium carbonate ($K_2CO_3$), and the alkyl or aryl group migrates from the carbonyl carbon to the nitrogen atom. The $-CO-$ group is not reduced to a $-CH_2-$ group. The reduction of an amide to an amine where the $-CO-$ group becomes a $-CH_2-$ group is achieved using strong reducing agents like $LiAlH_4$.

Since the product amine has one carbon less than the reactant amide, its molar mass is always less than that of the amide.

Thus, the statement that the $-CO-$ group is reduced to a $-CH_2-$ group is false.

Answer: In this -CO-group is reduced to $-\text{CH}_2-$ group.

56620.subject: Chemistry
56620.text: Which element from following is NOT regarded as transition element ?
56620.sol:
A transition element is defined as an element that has an incompletely filled d-orbital in its ground state or in any of its common oxidation states.

Cadmium ($\text{Cd}$) belongs to group 12 and has the ground state electronic configuration $[\text{Kr}] 4d^{10} 5s^{2}$. In its common oxidation state of $+2$, its configuration is $[\text{Kr}] 4d^{10}$. Since the d-orbitals are completely filled in both its ground state and its stable oxidation state, $\text{Cd}$ is not regarded as a transition element.

Copper ($\text{Cu}$) and Gold ($\text{Au}$) have incompletely filled d-orbitals in their $+2$ and $+3$ oxidation states respectively, while Scandium ($\text{Sc}$) has an incompletely filled d-orbital in its ground state.

Answer: $\text{Cd}$

59118.text:
An aqueous solution has an osmotic pressure of $4.92$ atm at $300$ K.
Calculate the molarity of the solution.
(R = 0.082$ L atm mol^{-1}$ K^{-1}$)$
59118.sol:
Using the formula for osmotic pressure:

$\pi = CRT$

Where $\pi$ is the osmotic pressure, $C$ is the molarity, $R$ is the gas constant, and $T$ is the temperature.

Substituting the given values:

$4.92 = C \times 0.082 \times 300$

$4.92 = C \times 24.6$

$C = \dfrac{4.92}{24.6} = 0.2$ M

Answer: $0.2$ M

Equation of tangent to parabola. Given $y^2 = 4x$ with $a=1$, the general tangent above the X-axis is $y = mx + \frac{1}{m}$, with $m > 0$.

Condition for circle tangency. Circle $(x-3)^2 + y^2 = 9$ has center $(3,0)$ and radius $3$. A line is tangent if the perpendicular distance from center to line equals $3$. For the line in form $mx - y + \frac{1}{m} = 0$, this distance is $\frac{|3m + \frac{1}{m}|}{\sqrt{m^2 + 1}} = 3$.

Since $m > 0$ and $3m^2+1 > 0$, the equation simplifies to $\frac{3m^2 + 1}{m\sqrt{m^2 + 1}} = 3$.

Squaring both sides and simplifying yields $3m^2 = 1$, so $m = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ (taking positive root).

Substituting gives the tangent $y = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x + \sqrt{3}$, which simplifies to $x - \sqrt{3}y + 3 = 0$. This has irrational coefficients, while all options are integer-coefficient lines. Option A is selected as no exact match exists.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

63569.subject: Mathematics
63569.text: Three numbers are chosen from 1 to 30. The probability that minimum is 10 and maximum is 26 is _______
63569.sol:
Total number of ways to select 3 numbers from 30 is ^{30}C_{3}$.

^{30}C_{3} = \dfrac{30 \times 29 \times 28}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 4060$

For the minimum to be 10 and the maximum to be 26, two of the selected numbers must be exactly 10 and 26.

The third number must be chosen from the integers strictly between 10 and 26.

The integers between 10 and 26 are 11, 12, ..., 25.

The number of such integers is $26 - 10 - 1 = 15$.

Thus, the number of favorable selections is 15.

The required probability is $\dfrac{15}{4060} = \dfrac{3}{812}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{812}$

63630.text: If $A$ and $B$ are independent events such that $P\left(A \cap B^{\prime}\right)=\frac{3}{25}$ and $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{A}^{\prime} \cap \mathrm{B}\right)=\frac{8}{25}$, then $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})=$
63630.sol:
Let $P(A) = x$ and $P(B) = y$, with $A$ and $B$ independent.
Given $P(A \cap B') = \frac{3}{25}$ and $P(A' \cap B) = \frac{8}{25}$, use independence: $P(A \cap B') = P(A)P(B')$ and $P(A' \cap B) = P(A')P(B)$.

Substituting $P(B') = 1 - y$ and $P(A') = 1 - x$:

$x(1 - y) = \frac{3}{25} \quad \Rightarrow \quad x - xy = \frac{3}{25}$

$y(1 - x) = \frac{8}{25} \quad \Rightarrow \quad y - xy = \frac{8}{25}$

Subtracting yields:

$(y - xy) - (x - xy) = \frac{8}{25} - \frac{3}{25} \quad \Rightarrow \quad y - x = \frac{1}{5} \quad \Rightarrow \quad y = x + \frac{1}{5}$

Substitute into the first equation:

$x(1 - (x + \frac{1}{5})) = \frac{3}{25} \quad \Rightarrow \quad x(\frac{4}{5} - x) = \frac{3}{25}$

Multiply both sides by 25:

$25x(\frac{4}{5} - x) = 3 \quad \Rightarrow \quad 20x - 25x^2 = 3$

Rearrange to standard form:

$25x^2 - 20x + 3 = 0$

Factor:

$(5x - 1)(5x - 3) = 0$

Solutions: $x = \frac{1}{5}$ or $x = \frac{3}{5}$

Both satisfy $P(A \cap B') = \frac{3}{25}$ and $P(A' \cap B) = \frac{8}{25}$ when $y = x + \frac{1}{5}$.
Among the options, only $\frac{1}{5}$ is listed.

$\boxed{\text{C}}$

64476.text: The distance of the point $(2,4,0)$ from the point of intersection of the lines $\frac{x+6}{3}=\frac{y}{2}=\frac{z+1}{1}$ and $\frac{x-7}{4}=\frac{y-9}{3}=\frac{z-4}{2}$ is
64476.sol:
A point on the first line can be expressed in parametric form as $x = 3\lambda - 6$, $y = 2\lambda$, $z = \lambda - 1$. The second line has parameterization $x = 4\mu + 7$, $y = 3\mu + 9$, $z = 2\mu + 4$.

Equating coordinates at the intersection point yields the system:

$3\lambda - 4\mu = 13$

$2\lambda - 3\mu = 9$

$\lambda - 2\mu = 5$

From the third equation, $\lambda = 2\mu + 5$. Substituting into the second gives $2(2\mu + 5) - 3\mu = 9$, which simplifies to $\mu = -1$. Then $\lambda = 2(-1) + 5 = 3$.

These values satisfy all equations, giving the intersection point $I(3, 6, 2)$.

The distance from $Q(2, 4, 0)$ to $I$ is $\sqrt{(3-2)^2 + (6-4)^2 + (2-0)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{9} =$3$.

65079.text: If $|\bar{a}| = |\bar{b}| = 1, |\bar{c}| = 2$ and $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$, then the acute angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $\ldots$
65079.sol:
Given $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

Using the vector triple product expansion:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a})\bar{c} + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

Since $|\bar{a}| = 1$, we have $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a} = 1$.

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} - \bar{c} + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

$\bar{b} = \bar{c} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a}$

Squaring both sides:

$|\bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{c}|^2 + (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2|\bar{a}|^2 - 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})$

Substituting $|\bar{a}| = 1$, $|\bar{b}| = 1$, and $|\bar{c}| = 2$:

$1 = 4 + (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2 - 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2$

$1 = 4 - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2$

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2 = 3$

Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{c}$. Then $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = |\bar{a}||\bar{c}|\cos\theta = 2\cos\theta$.

$(2\cos\theta)^2 = 3$

$4\cos^2\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \cos^2\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Since $\theta$ is an acute angle, $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

66062.text: Two identical metal plates are given charges $\mathrm{q}_1$ and $\mathrm{q}_{2} \left(\mathrm{q}_{2} < \mathrm{q}_{1}\right) respectively. If they are now brought close together to form a parallel plate capacitor with capacitance 'C', the potential difference 'V' between the plates is$
66062.sol:
When two identical metal plates with charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ form a parallel plate capacitor, the charges redistribute such that the outer surfaces carry equal charges $Q_{\text{outer}} = \frac{q_1 + q_2}{2}$ due to symmetry.

The inner surface charges are then $Q_{\text{inner1}} = q_1 - \frac{q_1 + q_2}{2} = \frac{q_1 - q_2}{2}$ and $Q_{\text{inner2}} = q_2 - \frac{q_1 + q_2}{2} = \frac{q_2 - q_1}{2}$, satisfying $Q_{\text{inner1}} = -Q_{\text{inner2}}$ as required.

The effective charge governing the electric field is $Q_{\text{eff}} = |Q_{\text{inner1}}| = \frac{|q_1 - q_2|}{2}$.
Given $q_2 < q_1$, this simplifies to $Q_{\text{eff}} = \frac{q_1 - q_2}{2}$.

The potential difference is then $V = \frac{Q_{\text{eff}}}{C} = \frac{q_1 - q_2}{2C}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

66997.text: Two electric dipoles of moment $P$ and $8P$ are placed in opposite directions on a line at a distance of $24$ cm. The electric field will be zero at the point between the dipoles whose distance from the dipole of moment $P$ will be $x_1$. When $8P$ is replaced by $27P$ keeping all other quantities the same, the distance $x_1$ now becomes $x_2$. The difference $|x_2 - x_1|$ is ( All the distances are measured from the centers of the dipole.)
66997.sol:
Let the distance of the null point from the dipole of moment $P$ be $x$. The distance from the second dipole is $24 - x$.

The electric field due to a short dipole on its axis at a distance $r$ is given by $E = \dfrac{2kP}{r^3}$.

For the net electric field to be zero, the magnitudes of the electric fields due to both dipoles must be equal.

Case 1: Dipoles are $P$ and $8P$
$\dfrac{2kP}{x_1^3} = \dfrac{2k(8P)}{(24 - x_1)^3}$

Taking the cube root on both sides:
$\dfrac{1}{x_1} = \dfrac{2}{24 - x_1}$

$24 - x_1 = 2x_1 \Rightarrow 3x_1 = 24 \Rightarrow x_1 = 8$ cm

Case 2: Dipole $8P$ is replaced by $27P$
$\dfrac{2kP}{x_2^3} = \dfrac{2k(27P)}{(24 - x_2)^3}$

Taking the cube root on both sides:
$\dfrac{1}{x_2} = \dfrac{3}{24 - x_2}$

$24 - x_2 = 3x_2 \Rightarrow 4x_2 = 24 \Rightarrow x_2 = 6$ cm

The difference is $|x_2 - x_1| = |6 - 8| = 2$ cm.

Answer: $2$ cm

67912.text: The magnetic field (B) inside a long solenoid having ' n ' turns per unit length and carrying current ' $i$ ' when iron core is kept in it, is (\mu_0=$ permeability of vacuum, \chi=$ magnetic susceptibility)
67912.sol:
Magnetic field enhancement in a solenoid with an iron core

The magnetic field inside a long solenoid with n turns per unit length carrying current i is given by $B_0 = \mu_0 n i$.

Introducing an iron core changes the permeability from $\mu_0$ to $\mu$, so the field becomes $B = \mu n i$.

The permeability of a magnetic material is defined by $\mu = \mu_0 (1 + \chi)$, where $\chi$ is the magnetic susceptibility.

Substituting this into the equation for the magnetic field yields $B = \mu_0 (1 + \chi) n i$.

68657.text: Two particles A and B of equal masses are suspended from two massless springs of spring constants $K_A$ and $K_B$ respectively. The maximum velocities of the particles during oscillations are equal. The ratio of the amplitude of 'B' to that of 'A' is
68657.sol:
Let the masses of the particles be $m$.

The angular frequencies of oscillations for particles A and B are $\omega_A = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_A}{m}}$ and $\omega_B = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_B}{m}}$.

The maximum velocity of a particle in simple harmonic motion is given by $v_\max = A \omega$, where $A$ is the amplitude.

Given that the maximum velocities are equal:

$A_A \omega_A = A_B \omega_B$

$A_A \sqrt{\dfrac{K_A}{m}} = A_B \sqrt{\dfrac{K_B}{m}}$

$A_A \sqrt{K_A} = A_B \sqrt{K_B}$

$\dfrac{A_B}{A_A} = \dfrac{\sqrt{K_A}}{\sqrt{K_B}}$

The ratio of the amplitude of B to that of A is $\sqrt{K_A} : \sqrt{K_B}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{K_A} : \sqrt{K_B}$

68670.text: For a particle P performing S.H.M., when displacement is 'x', potential energy and restoring force acting on it is denoted by 'E' and 'F' respectively. The relation between x, E and F is
68670.sol:
For a particle performing Simple Harmonic Motion (S.H.M.), the restoring force $F$ acting on it at a displacement $x$ is given by:

$F = -kx$

The potential energy $E$ of the particle at displacement $x$ is given by:

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^2$

Dividing the expression for potential energy by the expression for restoring force, we get:

$\dfrac{E}{F} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}kx^2}{-kx}$

$\dfrac{E}{F} = -\dfrac{x}{2}$

Rearranging the terms, we obtain:

$\dfrac{2E}{F} = -x$

$\dfrac{2E}{F} + x = 0$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\text{E}}{\text{F}} + x = 0$

69708.text: A body cools from a temperature $3\theta$ to $2\theta$ in 10 minute. The room temperature is $\theta$. The temperature of the body at the end of the next 10 minute is '$x$'. Assuming that Newton's law of cooling is applicable, the value of '$x$' will be
69708.sol:
According to Newton's law of cooling, the temperature $T$ of a body at time $t$ is given by:

$T - T_0 = (T_i - T_0)e^{-kt}$

where $T_0$ is the surrounding temperature and $T_i$ is the initial temperature.

For the first 10 minutes, $T_i = 3\theta$, $T = 2\theta$, and $T_0 = \theta$:

$2\theta - \theta = (3\theta - \theta)e^{-10k}$

$\theta = 2\theta e^{-10k}$

$e^{-10k} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

For the next 10 minutes, the new initial temperature is $T_i = 2\theta$ and the final temperature is $x$:

$x - \theta = (2\theta - \theta)e^{-10k}$

$x - \theta = \theta \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$x = \theta + $\dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}\theta

Answer: \dfrac{3}{2}\theta$

69724.text: About black body radiation, which one of the following is a WRONG statement?
options: For all wavelengths, power radiated is same
For shorter wavelengths, radiated power is more
for longer wavelengths, radiated power is less
All wavelengths are emitted by the black body
69724.sol:
According to the spectral distribution of black body radiation (Planck's law), a black body emits radiation of all possible wavelengths, but the energy is not uniformly distributed among them.

The spectral emissive power (E_{\lambda}$) first increases with an increase in wavelength, reaches a maximum value at a specific wavelength (\lambda_{m}$), and then decreases for longer wavelengths.

Therefore, the statement "For all wavelengths, power radiated is same" is completely incorrect.

Answer: For all wavelengths, power radiated is same

70461.subject: Physics
70461.text: A tuning fork of frequency $n$ produces $x$ beats per second when sounded with a vibrating sonometer string. What must have been the frequency of the string, when a slight increase in tension produces lesser beats per second than before?
70461.sol:
Let the frequency of the tuning fork be $n$ and the frequency of the sonometer string be $f$.

The number of beats per second is given by $x = |f - n|$.

This implies $f = n + x$ or $f = n - x$.

The frequency of a sonometer string is directly proportional to the square root of its tension (f \propto $\sqrt{T}).

When the tension in the string is slightly increased, its frequency $f$ increases.

If $f = n + x$, an increase in $f$ will increase the difference $|f - n|$, resulting in more beats per second.

If $f = n - x$, a slight increase in $f$ will decrease the difference $|f - n|$, resulting in fewer beats per second.

Since the number of beats per second decreases, the initial frequency of the string must have been $n - x$.$

70485.subject: Physics
70485.text: At poles, a stretched wire of a given length vibrates in unison with a tuning fork. At the equator, for same setting, to produce resonance with same fork, the vibrating length of wire
70485.sol:
The frequency of a vibrating stretched wire is given by $f = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}$, where $L$ is the wire length, $T$ is the tension, and $\mu$ is the linear mass density. For resonance with the same tuning fork, $f$ remains constant, and $\mu$ is unchanged.

The tension $T$ equals the weight of the hanging mass, so $T = mg$. At the poles, $g$ is unchanged, but at the equator, the effective gravity is reduced to $g - R\omega^2$, where $R$ is Earth's radius and $\omega$ is its angular velocity. Consequently, $T_{\text{equator}} = m(g - R\omega^2) < T_{\text{pole}} = mg$.

Since $f \propto \frac{1}{L}\sqrt{T}$ and $f$ is constant, $L \propto \sqrt{T}$. With $T_{\text{equator}} < T_{\text{pole}}$, it follows that $\sqrt{T_{\text{equator}}} < \sqrt{T_{\text{pole}}}$, so $L_{\text{equator}} < L_{\text{pole}}$ to maintain the same frequency.

Thus, the vibrating length must be decreased, and the correct choice is $\boxed{A}$.

71562.subject: Biology
71562.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Due to endo-osmosis water from surrounding cells and xylem, is absorbed.
Statement (II): Due to decrease in turgor pressure, sugar from photosynthetic cell is forced ultimately into sieve tube of vein
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below with reference to mechanism of sugar transport through phloem.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71562.sol:
According to the mass flow hypothesis for the mechanism of sugar transport in phloem, glucose prepared at the source is converted into sucrose and actively transported into the companion cells and then into the sieve tube cells. This active loading creates a hypertonic condition in the phloem.

Statement (I) is correct because the hypertonic condition in the sieve tubes causes water from the adjacent xylem and surrounding cells to move into the phloem by endosmosis.

Statement (II) is incorrect because sugar is loaded into the sieve tube by active transport, not due to a decrease in turgor pressure. In fact, the entry of water by endosmosis builds up a high turgor pressure inside the sieve tube, which forces the phloem sap to move towards the sink where turgor pressure is lower.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect

71797.subject: Chemistry
71797.text: What is the IUPAC name of the following compound?
71797.sol:
The principal functional group in the given compound is the hydroxyl group ($-OH$), which has higher priority for nomenclature than the halogen group ($-Br$).

The longest continuous carbon chain contains 7 carbon atoms, so the parent alkane is heptane.

The carbon chain must be numbered from the end that gives the lowest possible locant to the principal functional group. Numbering from right to left assigns position 3 to the $-OH$ group and position 6 to the $-Br$ group. Numbering from left to right would assign position 5 to the $-OH$ group, which is incorrect.

With the bromo substituent at position 6 and the alcohol suffix at position 3, the IUPAC name is 6-bromoheptan-3-ol.

Answer: 6-Bromoheptan-3-ol

73772.subject: General Ability
73772.text: For an object in gravitational field, the gravitational potential is the same at two points $A$ and $B$, but the gravitational field is not the same at these two points. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Positive work is done by gravity in moving the object from point $A$ to point $B$.
Negative work is done by gravity in moving the object from point $A$ to point $B$.
Gravity must be non-conservative in such a region.
No work is done by gravity in moving the object from point $A$ to point $B$.
73772.sol:
The work done by the gravitational force on an object of mass $m$ in moving it from point $A$ to point $B$ is given by $W = -\Delta U = -m(V_B - V_A) = m(V_A - V_B)$, where $V_A$ and $V_B$ are the gravitational potentials at points $A$ and $B$ respectively.

It is given that the gravitational potential is the same at points $A$ and $B$, which means $V_A = V_B$.

Substituting this into the work equation, we get $W = m(V_A - V_A) = 0$.

The difference in the gravitational field at the two points does not affect the total work done between these equipotential points, as gravity is a conservative force and work done is independent of the path taken.

Therefore, no work is done by gravity in moving the object from point $A$ to point $B$.

options: Light travels at different speeds in different media.
Light travels at almost 300 million metres per second in air.
Light speeds down as it leaves a water surface and enters the air.
Light speeds up as it leaves a glass surface and enters the air.
74164.sol:
A light ray is a line (straight or curved) that is perpendicular to the light's wavefronts; its tangent is collinear with the wave vector. Light rays in homogeneous media are straight. They bend at the interface between two dissimilar media and may be curved in a medium in which the refractive index changes
Light waves travel fastest through a vacuum and air, and slower through other materials such as glass or water. Light travels at approximately 300,000 kilometers per second in a vacuum, which has a refractive index of 1.0 , but it slows down to 225,000 kilometers per second in water and 200,000 kilometers per second in glass.

77038.sol:
$y^2=2 c x+2 c \sqrt{c}$
Differentiate wrt $x$,
$2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=2 c\Rightarrow \quad c=y \frac{d y}{d x}\Rightarrow \quad y^2=2 x \cdot y \frac{d y}{d x}+2\left(y \frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{3 / 2}\Rightarrow y^2-2 x y \frac{d y}{d x}=2 \cdot\left(y \frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{3 / 2}$
Squaring both sides,
$y^4+4 x^2 y^2\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2-4 x y^3 \frac{d y}{d x}=4 y^3\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^3$
Clearly order $=1$.

Which one of the following ions is the most stable in aqueous solution?

\mathrm{ V}^{3+}(20) & =3 d^2 4 s^0 \Rightarrow t_{28}{ }^2 e_g^0 \\

\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}(22) & =3 d^4 4 s^0 \Rightarrow t_{2 g}{ }^4 e_g^0

82977.subject: Physics
82977.text: An electron moves in a circular orbit with a uniform speed $v$. It produces a magnetic field $B$ at the centre of the circle. The radius of the circle is proportional to:
82977.sol:
The magnetic field \((B)\) at a point induced by a flowing current \((I)\) is given as,
\(B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 r}\)
Where \(\mu_0\) is the permeability of free space, and \(r\) is the radius of the circular path.
Substituting for \(I\) and rearranging,
\(\begin{aligned}
& B=\frac{\mu_0\left(\frac{e v}{2 \pi r}\right)}{2 r} \\
\Rightarrow & B=\frac{\mu_0 e v}{4 \pi r^2} \\
\Rightarrow & r^2=\frac{\mu_0 e v}{4 \pi B} \\
\Rightarrow & r^2 \propto \frac{v}{B} \\
\therefore & r \propto \sqrt{\frac{v}{B}}
\end{aligned}\)
Therefore, when an electron moves in a circular orbit with a uniform speed \(v\) and produces a magnetic field \(B\) at the centre of the circle, the radius of the circle is proportional to \(\sqrt{\frac{v}{B}}\).

85164.subject: Zoology
85164.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : In an experiment, Mendel observed that the F1 progeny plants are all tall and none are dwarf.
Reason R : Stem height is a contrasting trait, with tall being dominant and dwarf being recessive.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: $\text{A}$ is not correct but $\text{R}$ is correct
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct but $\text{R}$ is not the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
$\text{A}$ is correct but $\text{R}$ is not correct
85164.sol:
Assertion A is correct because when Mendel crossed true-breeding tall pea plants with true-breeding dwarf pea plants, all the plants in the F1 generation were tall.

Reason R is correct and explains Assertion A. Stem height is a contrasting trait in pea plants where the tall trait is dominant over the dwarf trait. Since the F1 progeny are heterozygous, the dominant allele expresses itself, resulting in all tall plants.

Therefore, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$

89007.subject: Chemistry
89007.text:
What will be the value of x, y and $z$ in the following equation?
${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} + x{H}_{2}{O}_{2} \to yC{O}_{2} + z{H}_{2}O$
89007.sol:
(i) The half reaction for oxidation is,
${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to C{O}_{2}$
Balancing carbon atoms on both sides, ${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to 2C{O}_{2}$
Balancing hydrogen atoms on both sides, ${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to 2C{O}_{2} + 2H^{+}$
Balancing the charge on both sides,
${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to 2C{O}_{2} + 2H^{+} + 2e^{-}$...(i)
(ii) The half reaction for reduction is‐ ${H}_{2} {O}_{2} \to {H}_{2} \text{O}$
Balancing oxygen atoms on both sides, ${H}_{2}{O}_{2} \to 2{H}_{2}O$
Balancing hydrogen atoms, ${H}_{2}{O}_{2} + 2H^{+} \to 2{H}_{2}O$
Balancing the charge,
${H}_{2}{O}_{2} + 2H^{+} + 2e^{-} \to 2{H}_{2}O$...(ii)
Now, adding both equations, ${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} + {H}_{2}{O}_{2} \to 2C{O}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$
This is balanced equation so x, y, z are 1,2,2 respectively.

Let,& $\alpha = \beta - d$ and $\gamma = \beta + d$
$\beta - d, \beta, \beta + d$ are the roots

$⇒$ The roots are $- 7, - 2,3$
$⇒ \left|\alpha\right| + \left|\beta\right| + \left|\gamma\right| = 12$

92876.text: When a battery of emf $8V$ with internal resistance $0.5Ω$ is charged by a $120VDC$ supply using a series resistance of $15.5Ω$, then what is the terminal voltage (in volt) of the battery?

Here, emf of the battery $= 8V$

The internal resistance of the battery, $r = 0.5Ω$

The voltage of D. C supply = $120V$

External resistance, $R = 15.5Ω$

When the battery of emf $8V$ is charged from a $DC$ supply of $120V$, the effective emf in the circular is

$ε = 120 - 8 = 112V$

The total resistance of the circuit $= R + r$

$= \left(15.5 + 0.5\right)Ω = 16Ω$

$∴$ Current in the circuit during charging

$I = \dfrac{ε}{R + r} = \dfrac{112}{16} = 7A$

$∴$ The terminal voltage of the battery,

$V = emfofthebattery + voltagedropacrossthebattery$

$= 8 + Ir = 8 + 7\left(0.5\right) = 11.5V$

options: Overcoming apical dominance and helps in sprouting of lateral buds
97279.sol: Apical dominance has been explained as due to the action of auxin present in the main apex. This view is amply supported by an experiment, where if the stem tip is cut off, the axillary buds found below sprout immediately. Instead, if an agar block containing auxin placed over the decapitated stem, the axillary buds remain suppressed. It is clear from the above experiment, that auxin present in the main apex somehow inhibits the growth of the axillary bud. The severity of apical dominance is greater on the axillary buds present nearer to the main apex. Nevertheless, apical dominance exerted by the auxins can be overcome by the application of cytokinin to axillary buds. This is because cytokinin induces cytokinesis

97762.sol: The TCA cycle or the Kreb's cycle is a form of aerobic respiration where the reaction starts with the acetyl group condensation by oxaloacetic acid and water, whose product is citric acid. The citrate is then isomerised to isocitrate followed by successive steps of decarboxylation. The first step of decarboxylation leads to the formation of a 5-C dicarboxylic acid, the $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid which is used in nitrogen metabolism as a precursor for many amino acids and purines.

102661.subject: Physics
102661.text: An open organ pipe of length $40\text{ cm}$ and a closed organ pipe of length $50\text{ cm}$ are sounded together. If the $1^{\text{st}}$ overtone of the open pipe resonates with the $n^{\text{th}}$ overtone of the closed pipe, what is the value of $n$? (Assume the speed of sound is the same in both pipes and ignore end corrections).
102661.sol:
For an open organ pipe of length $L_o$, the frequency of the $1^{\text{st}}$ overtone (which is the $2^{\text{nd}}$ harmonic) is given by:
$f_o = 2 \left( \dfrac{v}{2L_o} \right) = \dfrac{v}{L_o}$

For a closed organ pipe of length $L_c$, the frequency of the $n^{\text{th}}$ overtone (which is the $(2n+1)^{\text{th}}$ harmonic) is given by:
$f_c = (2n+1) \left( \dfrac{v}{4L_c} \right)$

Given that these two frequencies are equal:
$\dfrac{v}{L_o} = \dfrac{(2n+1)v}{4L_c}$

Substitute $L_o = 40\text{ cm}$ and $L_c = 50\text{ cm}$:
$\dfrac{v}{40} = \dfrac{(2n+1)v}{4 \times 50}$

$\dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{2n+1}{200}$

$2n+1 = \dfrac{200}{40} = 5$

$2n = 4 \Rightarrow n = 2$

Answer: $2$

103931.subject: Physics
103931.text: The magnitude of the induced emf in a coil varies with time $t$ according to the equation $|e| = 4t + 2$ (where $e$ is in volts and $t$ is in seconds). The magnitude of the change in magnetic flux linked with the coil during the time interval from $t = 1\text{ s}$ to $t = 3\text{ s}$ is:
103931.sol:
From Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of induced emf is given by $|e| = \dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$.

This implies that the change in magnetic flux $d\Phi = |e| dt$.

To find the total change in magnetic flux $\Delta\Phi$ from $t = 1\text{ s}$ to $t = 3\text{ s}$, we integrate the emf equation:

$\Delta\Phi = \int_{1}^{3} (4t + 2) dt$

$\Delta\Phi = \left[ \dfrac{4t^2}{2} + 2t \right]_{1}^{3} = \left[ 2t^2 + 2t \right]_{1}^{3}$

Substituting the upper and lower limits:

$\Delta\Phi = \left( 2(3)^2 + 2(3) \right) - \left( 2(1)^2 + 2(1) \right)$

$\Delta\Phi = (18 + 6) - (2 + 2)$

$\Delta\Phi = 24 - 4 = 20\text{ Wb}$

Answer: $20\text{ Wb}$

104858.subject: Physics
104858.text: An electron in a hydrogen atom has a total energy of $-0.85 \text{ eV}$. What is the angular momentum of the electron in this state?
104858.sol:
The total energy of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by $E = \dfrac{-13.6}{n^2} \text{ eV}$.

Given $E = -0.85 \text{ eV}$, we have:
$\dfrac{-13.6}{n^2} = -0.85$
$n^2 = \dfrac{13.6}{0.85} = 16$
$n = 4$

According to Bohr's postulate, the angular momentum of the electron is $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.

Substituting $n = 4$, we get:
$L = \dfrac{4h}{2\pi} = \dfrac{2h}{\pi}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2h}{\pi}$
104858.meta: An electron in a hydrogen atom has a total energy of -0.85 eV . What is the angular momentum of the electron in this state?

105438.subject: Physics
105438.text: The least count of a vernier callipers is given as $x$ mm. It is observed that $N$ divisions of its vernier scale coincide exactly with $(N-2)$ divisions of the main scale. The value of one main scale division ($1\text{ MSD}$) is:
105438.sol:
The least count (LC) of a vernier callipers is defined as:
$\text{LC} = 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD}$

Given the coincidence relation:
$N\text{ VSD} = (N-2)\text{ MSD}$
$1\text{ VSD} = \dfrac{N-2}{N}\text{ MSD}$

Substitute this into the least count formula:
$\text{LC} = 1\text{ MSD} - \left(\dfrac{N-2}{N}\right)\text{ MSD}$
$\text{LC} = \left(1 - \dfrac{N-2}{N}\right)\text{ MSD}$
$\text{LC} = \left(\dfrac{N - N + 2}{N}\right)\text{ MSD} = \dfrac{2}{N}\text{ MSD}$

We are given that $\text{LC} = x$. Therefore:
$x = \dfrac{2}{N}\text{ MSD}$

Rearranging to find the value of $1\text{ MSD}$:
$1\text{ MSD} = \dfrac{Nx}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Nx}{2}$

105890.subject: Chemistry
105890.text:
A $5.0\text{ g}$ sample of impure calcium carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$) containing $80\%$ pure $\text{CaCO}_3$ by mass is allowed to react with $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.45\text{ M}$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution. What will be the mass of $\text{CO}_2$ gas formed upon complete reaction?

$\text{CaCO}_{3(\text{s})} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_{4(\text{aq})} \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_{4(\text{aq})} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(\text{l})} + \text{CO}_{2(\text{g})}$
105890.sol:
The balanced chemical equation is:
$\text{CaCO}_{3(\text{s})} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_{4(\text{aq})} \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_{4(\text{aq})} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(\text{l})} + \text{CO}_{2(\text{g})}$

Moles of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ available $= \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume (in L)}$
$= 0.45 \times 0.100 = 0.045\text{ mol}$

Mass of pure $\text{CaCO}_3$ in the sample $= 5.0 \times \dfrac{80}{100} = 4.0\text{ g}$
Molar mass of $\text{CaCO}_3 = 100\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of pure $\text{CaCO}_3$ available $= \dfrac{4.0}{100} = 0.040\text{ mol}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{CaCO}_3$ reacts with $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
Since $0.040\text{ mol}$ of $\text{CaCO}_3$ is less than $0.045\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $\text{CaCO}_3$ is the limiting reagent.

Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ produced $= \text{Moles of limiting reagent } (\text{CaCO}_3) = 0.040\text{ mol}$
Mass of $\text{CO}_2$ produced $= 0.040 \times 44 = 1.76\text{ g}$

Answer: $1.76\text{ g}$

116333.subject: Chemistry
116333.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the hydrides of Group 17 elements:
(I) The thermal stability of the hydrides follows the order $\mathrm{HF} > \mathrm{HCl} > \mathrm{HBr} > \mathrm{HI}$.
(II) The reducing power of the hydrides follows the order $\mathrm{HF} < \mathrm{HCl} < \mathrm{HBr} < \mathrm{HI}$.
(III) The boiling points of the hydrides follow the order $\mathrm{HCl} < \mathrm{HBr} < \mathrm{HI} < \mathrm{HF}$.
(IV) The acidic strength of the hydrides follows the order $\mathrm{HI} > \mathrm{HBr} > \mathrm{HCl} > \mathrm{HF}$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
116333.sol:
Statement (I) is correct: Thermal stability decreases down the group as the $\mathrm{H-X}$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases from $\mathrm{HF}$ to $\mathrm{HI}$.

Statement (II) is correct: Reducing power increases down the group because the decreasing bond enthalpy makes it easier to release hydrogen.

Statement (III) is correct: $\mathrm{HF}$ has an anomalously high boiling point due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. For the other hydrogen halides, the boiling point increases with molecular mass due to increasing magnitude of van der Waals forces.

Statement (IV) is correct: Acidic strength increases down the group as the $\mathrm{H-X}$ bond becomes weaker and easier to break in aqueous solution.

Therefore, all four statements are correct.

Answer: Four

116334.subject: Chemistry
116334.text: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the elements of Group 16.
options: The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond is stronger than the $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}$ single bond.
Oxygen shows a much lower tendency for catenation than sulphur.
Sulphur can form $\mathrm{d} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ multiple bonds whereas oxygen cannot.
Oxygen cannot expand its covalency beyond four due to the absence of d-orbitals.
116334.sol:
The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond is weaker than the $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}$ single bond because of high interelectronic repulsion between the lone pairs of electrons on the small oxygen atoms. Thus, the statement claiming it is stronger is incorrect.

Due to the weaker $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond, oxygen has a much lower tendency for catenation compared to sulphur.

Sulphur has vacant d-orbitals and can form $\mathrm{d} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ multiple bonds, while oxygen is restricted to $\mathrm{p} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ bonding due to the absence of d-orbitals.

The absence of d-orbitals in the valence shell of oxygen limits its covalency to a maximum of four.

Answer: The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond is stronger than the $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}$ single bond.

118269.subject: Chemistry
118269.text: An unknown alkyl halide 'X' undergoes substitution with KCN, followed by acidic hydrolysis to form an intermediate. This intermediate on treatment with $\text{Br}_2$/Red P followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ yields 2-bromobutanoic acid as the major product. Identify the starting alkyl halide 'X'.
118269.sol:
The final product is 2-bromobutanoic acid, which is formed via the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction.

Working backwards, the intermediate carboxylic acid before the HVZ reaction must be butanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$).

Butanoic acid is formed by the acidic hydrolysis of butanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$).

Since the reaction of an alkyl halide with KCN involves a step-up of one carbon atom, the starting alkyl halide 'X' must contain 3 carbon atoms in a straight chain.

Therefore, 'X' is 1-chloropropane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$).

Reaction sequence:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{(i) } \text{Br}_2\text{/Red P}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{COOH}$

Answer: 1-Chloropropane

121039.subject: Chemistry
121039.text:
Assertion : A solution of sucrose in water is dextrorotatory. But on hydrolysis in the presence of a little hydrochloric acid, it becomes laevorotatory.
Reason : Sucrose on hydrolysis gives unequal amounts of glucose and fructose. As a result of this, change in sign of rotation is observed.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
121039.sol:
The hydrolysis of sucrose by boiling with a mineral acid $(\mathrm{HCl})$, produces a mixture of equal molecules of $D$-glucose and $D$-fructose. Sucrose solution is dextrorotatory, specific rotation $=+66.5^{\circ}$. But on hydrolysis, it becomes laevorotatory. The specific rotation of $D$-glucose is $+52^{\circ}$ and of $D$-fructose is $-92^{\circ}$. Therefore, the net specific rotation of an equimolar mixture of both is :
$\frac{+52^{\circ}-92^{\circ}}{2}=-20^{\circ}$
$\therefore \quad$ laevorotatory.

121706.subject: Botany
121706.text: Which algae is known to have a filamentous form?
121706.sol: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms. They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soils and wood. Some of them also occur in association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g., on sloth bear). <mark>The form and size of algae is highly variable, ranging from colonial forms like Volvox and the filamentous forms like Ulothrix and Spirogyra</mark> (Figure 3.1). A few of the marine forms such as kelps, form massive plant bodies.The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

122534.subject: Botany
122534.text:
Read the following statements regarding the members of Class Reptilia:

(i) They are mostly terrestrial animals and their body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes.
(ii) They do not have external ear openings; the tympanum represents the ear.
(iii) The heart is usually three-chambered, but four-chambered in crocodiles.
(iv) Fertilisation is internal, they are oviparous and development is indirect.

How many of the above statements are correct?
122534.sol:
Statement (i) is correct. Reptiles are mostly terrestrial animals and their body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes.

Statement (ii) is correct. Reptiles do not have external ear openings; the tympanum represents the ear.

Statement (iii) is correct. The heart is usually three-chambered in reptiles, but crocodiles are an exception and have a four-chambered heart.

Statement (iv) is incorrect. While fertilisation is internal and they are oviparous, development in reptiles is direct, meaning there is no larval stage.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

122545.subject: Botany
122545.text: A marine vertebrate migrates to fresh water for spawning. After spawning, within a few days, it dies. Its larvae, after metamorphosis, return to the ocean. Which of the following morphological features is characteristic of this animal?
options: Presence of placoid scales and claspers in males
Body is devoid of scales and paired fins
Presence of ctenoid scales and an air bladder
122545.sol:
The life cycle described (migration to fresh water for spawning, death after spawning, and larval metamorphosis before returning to the ocean) is a characteristic feature of class Cyclostomata (e.g., Petromyzon).

Members of Cyclostomata have an elongated body, a sucking and circular mouth without jaws, and their body is devoid of scales and paired fins.

Placoid scales and claspers are features of Chondrichthyes.

Ctenoid scales and an air bladder are features of Osteichthyes.

A three-chambered heart and moist skin are features of Amphibia.

Answer: Body is devoid of scales and paired fins

122570.subject: Botany
122570.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the features of different animal phyla.

List-IList-II
A. Mesoderm as scattered pouches1. Platyhelminthes
B. Body cavity lined by mesoderm2. Aschelminthes
C. Absence of body cavity3. Annelida
D. Cellular level of organization4. Porifera

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
122570.sol:
In Aschelminthes, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called a pseudocoelom. Thus, A matches with 2.

In Annelida, the body cavity is lined by mesoderm, which is called a true coelom. Thus, B matches with 3.

In Platyhelminthes, the body cavity is absent, making them acoelomates. Thus, C matches with 1.

In Porifera, the animals exhibit a cellular level of organization. Thus, D matches with 4.

Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4.

Answer: A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4

124374.text: Read the following statements regarding the Golgi apparatus and choose the incorrect statement.
options: The Golgi apparatus consists of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae of $0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ to $1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter.

124374.sol:
The Golgi apparatus consists of flat, disc-shaped sacs called cisternae, which are $0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ to $1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ in diameter.

The organelle is distinctly polarised, with a convex cis (forming) face and a concave trans (maturing) face. These faces are entirely different but interconnected.

Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing (trans) face. Therefore, the statement claiming that vesicles fuse with the trans face and move towards the cis face is incorrect.

The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

125362.subject: Botany
125362.text: What is the absorption peak of the reaction center chlorophyll a in Photosystem II (PS II)?
125362.sol: Light reactions or the ‘Photochemical’ phase include light absorption, water splitting, oxygen release, and the formation of high-energy chemical intermediates, ATP and NADPH. Several protein complexes are involved in the process. The pigments are organised into two discrete photochemical light harvesting complexes (LHC) within the Photosystem I (PS I) and Photosystem II (PS II). These are named in the sequence of their discovery, and not in the sequence in which they function during the light reaction. The LHC are made up of hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins. Each photosystem has all the pigments (except one molecule of chlorophyll a) forming a light harvesting system also called antennae. These pigments help to make photosynthesis more efficient by absorbing different wavelengths of light. The single chlorophyll a molecule forms the reaction centre. The reaction centre is different in both the photosystems. In PS I the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm, hence is called P700, while in PS II it has absorption maxima at 680 nm, and is called P680.

125685.subject: Botany
125685.text:
Assertion : Cyclic photophosphorylation synthesises ATP.
Reason : ATP synthesis in cyclic photophosphorylation is associated with NADPH formation.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
125685.sol:
In case of cyclic photophosphorylation, the electron while passing between ferredoxin and plastoquinone and/or over the cytochrome complex, loses sufficient energy to form ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate.
In cyclic photophosphorylation no NADPH formation takes place. But in case of noncyclic photophosphorylation, NADP - reduced through $\mathrm{H}^{+}$released during photolysis forms NADPH. ATP synthesis is not direct and the energy released by electron is actually used for pumping $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions across the thylakoid membrane. It creates a proton gradient. The gradient triggers the coupling factor to synthesise ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate.

126531.sol: Polysaccharides are components of cell wall in plants, fungi and also of the exoskeleton of arthropods. They also are storage forms of energy (e.g., starch and glycogen). Plant cell walls are made of cellulose. Paper made from plant pulp and cotton fibre is cellulosic. There are more complex polysaccharides in nature. They have as building blocks, amino-sugars and chemically modified sugars (e.g., glucosamine, N-acetyl galactosamine, etc.). Exoskeletons of arthropods, for example, have a complex polysaccharide called chitin. These complex polysaccharides are mostly homopolymers.

127190.subject: Botany
127190.text: What is the difference between the current episode of extinction and previous episodes?
127190.sol: During the long period (> 3 billion years) since the origin and diversification of life on earth there were five episodes of mass extinction of species. How is the ‘Sixth Extinction’ presently in progress different from the previous episodes? The difference is in the rates; the current species extinction rates are estimated to be 100 to 1,000 times faster than in the pre-human times and our activities are responsible for the faster rates. Ecologists warn that if the present trends continue, nearly half of all the species on earth might be wiped out within the next 100 years

127196.subject: Botany
127196.text: What is the main cause of habitat loss and fragmentation?
127196.sol: In general, loss of biodiversity in a region may lead to (a) decline in plant production, (b) lowered resistance to environmental perturbations such as drought and (c) increased variability in certain ecosystem processes such as plant productivity, water use, and pest and disease cycles. Causes of biodiversity losses: The accelerated rates of species extinctions that the world is facing now are largely due to human activities. There are four major causes (‘ The Evil Quartet’ is the sobriquet used to describe them)
